content:
This seems to have slipped under the radar, but as far as I can tell, the cross-reference attributes like @[stacks] etc have been been meant to edit the docstring, but this has never really worked.

More specifically, if I have a declaration like:

import Mathlib.Tactic.CrossRefAttribute

/-- This docstring should appear before any Stacks or Kerodon references. -/
@[stacks A04Q "A comment", kerodon B15R "Also a comment"]
theorem taggedWithOwnDocstring : True := .intro

then

run_cmd Lean.logInfo m!"{← Lean.findDocString? (← Lean.getEnv) `taggedWithOwnDocstring}"

is going to result in only the original docstring, with no Stacks or Kerodon references. This is because the docstring extension is defined as .async .asyncEnv so the main thread (where attributes are evaluated) can't access the values from the async elaboration thread (where the docstring is evaluated).

Enabling Verso gives a seemingly opposite result, because Markdown docstrings (added by the attribute) take precedence over Verso docstrings (added on the declaration itself):

import Mathlib.Tactic.CrossRefAttribute

set_option doc.verso true in
/-- This docstring should appear before any Stacks or Kerodon references. -/
@[stacks A04Q "A comment", kerodon B15R "Also a comment"]
theorem versoTaggedWithOwnDocstring : True := .intro

/--
info: some ([Stacks Tag A04Q](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/A04Q) (A comment)

[Kerodon Tag B15R](https://kerodon.net/tag/B15R) (Also a comment))
 -/
#guard_msgs in
run_cmd Lean.logInfo m!"{← Lean.findDocString? (← Lean.getEnv) `versoTaggedWithOwnDocstring}"

Is it possible to fix the cross-reference attributes so they do the right thing with the docstring?

If not, we should be able to implement cross-references as special Verso roles (and still store the references in the environment, since docs#Lean.Doc.DocM extends docs#Lean.Elab.TermElabM). Does that sound like a good replacement? In the meantime, shall I "fix" the Verso behaviour by making it equally broken as Markdown?

In the meantime, shall I "fix" the Verso behaviour by making it equally broken as Markdown?

Since this wasn't working before, I think it's a completely fine "fix" to disable stuff so that the verso docstrings do not display any tag information either.
